testing: Rules were written for this project and tested in the Sentinel X in-browser Sigma evaluator against the 52 simulated log lines in sample-logs.json. They have NOT been validated with pySigma / sigma-cli or run against a production SIEM backend; status is therefore 'experimental'. Field names follow the Sigma taxonomy; tune filters for your environment before use.

rules.objective: Detect Office applications launching script interpreters or LOLBins, a common sign of a malicious macro.
investigation: Identify the document that was open (recent files, email attachment, download path)
Review the child process command line and any network connections it made
Check for files written and persistence created in the following minutes
Find other recipients of the same document
remediation: Isolate the host if the child process ran a payload
Enable the ASR rule 'Block all Office applications from creating child processes'
Block macros in files from the internet
yaml: title: Office Application Spawned Script Interpreter or LOLBin
description: Detects Microsoft Office applications starting script interpreters or proxy-execution binaries, which often indicates a malicious macro.
- Legitimate macros or add-ins that call scripts (document management, reporting tools)

rules.objective: Detect PowerShell started with an encoded command, which hides the real script from casual inspection.
investigation: Decode the Base64 (UTF-16LE) command
Correlate with PowerShell 4104 script-block logs for the decoded content
Check the parent process
remediation: Enable PowerShell script block logging everywhere
Use Constrained Language Mode and application control for non-admin users
yaml: description: Detects PowerShell launched with an encoded command line argument.
- Management agents and installers that pass encoded commands

rules.objective: Detect in-memory download-and-execute patterns recorded by PowerShell script block logging.
investigation: Extract the URL from the script block and check it against threat intel
Look for the corresponding network connection (Sysmon 3, proxy logs)
Identify any dropped files or follow-on processes
remediation: Block the download host at proxy and firewall
Isolate the host and collect memory
Restrict outbound internet access for workstations to the proxy
yaml: title: PowerShell Download Cradle in Script Block
description: Detects common in-memory download-and-execute patterns logged by Script Block Logging (event 4104).
- Administrative or software-deployment scripts that bootstrap from internal repositories

rules.objective: Detect processes opening LSASS with access rights commonly used to read credentials from memory.
investigation: Identify the source process, its signer and how it started
Check whether credentials from this host were used elsewhere afterwards
Collect memory and the source binary
remediation: Enable LSA protection (RunAsPPL) and Credential Guard
Reset credentials of accounts that were logged on to the host
Add confirmed security tools to the filter, nothing else
yaml: description: Detects a process outside system and program directories opening lsass.exe with access masks typical of credential dumping tools.
- Security and backup agents installed outside the filtered paths

rules.objective: Detect deletion of Volume Shadow Copies, a standard ransomware step to prevent recovery.
investigation: Identify the parent process and user
Look for mass file modification on the same host
Check other hosts for the same parent binary
remediation: Isolate the host immediately and confirm isolation is enforced
Verify offline backups
Hunt for the parent binary's hash across the estate
yaml: title: Shadow Copies Deleted via vssadmin or wmic
description: Detects deletion of Volume Shadow Copies with vssadmin or wmic, commonly done by ransomware before encryption.
- Backup software rotating its own shadow copies (verify the parent process)

rules.objective: Detect clearing of the Windows Security event log, an anti-forensics step.
investigation: Identify the account that cleared the log
Rebuild the missing period from the SIEM copy of forwarded events
Review that account's other activity
remediation: Forward logs off-host in near real time
Restrict who holds the 'Manage auditing and security log' right
yaml: description: Detects event 1102, written when the Windows Security audit log is cleared.
- Documented maintenance on lab or test systems

rules.objective: Surface every new user account so it can be matched against an approved change.
investigation: Check for a matching change ticket or HR request
Review the creating account's recent logons
Inspect group memberships given to the new account
remediation: Disable unapproved accounts immediately
Route account creation through an identity-management workflow
yaml: description: Detects event 4720 (a user account was created). Intended for review against change records rather than as a high-fidelity alert.
- Normal account provisioning by administrators or identity systems

rules.objective: Detect scheduled tasks created by a user account under the \Microsoft\Windows\ folder, where attackers hide persistence among built-in tasks.
investigation: Export the task XML and inspect the action path
Check the creating user and parent process
Look for the task's binary on other hosts
remediation: Delete the task and its binary
Alert on task actions pointing to user-writable paths
yaml: title: Scheduled Task Created Under Microsoft Folder by a User
description: Detects event 4698 for tasks whose name starts with \Microsoft\Windows\ when the creator is a user account rather than the computer account.
- Software installers run interactively that register tasks in this folder

rules.objective: Detect Run-key persistence pointing to user-writable locations such as Temp or AppData.
investigation: Identify the binary referenced by the value and its signer
Check what process set the value
Search for the binary on other hosts
remediation: Remove the value and the binary
Use application control to block execution from user-writable paths
yaml: title: Run Key Points to User-Writable Path
description: Detects Run or RunOnce registry values whose data points to Temp, AppData or Public folders.
- Per-user application updaters installed in AppData (allow-list known publishers)

rules.objective: Detect DNS queries whose first label is a long base32-style string, typical of DNS tunnelling or DNS-based C2.
investigation: Group queries by parent domain and count them
Identify the querying process (Sysmon 22 Image)
Check the domain's age and reputation
remediation: Sinkhole the domain on internal resolvers
Force DNS through monitored resolvers and block direct port 53
yaml: description: Detects Sysmon DNS query events where the first label is 25 or more characters from the base32 alphabet.
- CDNs and security products that encode identifiers in subdomains

rules.objective: Detect the same DNS tunnelling pattern in resolver logs, which also covers hosts without Sysmon.
investigation: Identify the client IP and map it to a host
Count queries per parent domain over time
Decode labels where possible to estimate data volume
remediation: Sinkhole the domain
Alert on TXT-query volume per client
yaml: title: TXT Query With Long Base32-Like Label (Resolver Log)
description: Detects TXT queries in DNS server logs where the first label is 25 or more base32-alphabet characters.
- Email security (SPF/DKIM) and anti-malware lookups using encoded TXT queries

rules.objective: Flag failed network logons from non-internal addresses. Single events are low severity; counting them is done by a correlation rule.
investigation: Count failures per source IP and user over time (see SIEM rule COR-001)
Check whether any logon from the same source succeeded
Find out why the service is reachable from outside
remediation: Remove internet exposure of SMB/RDP
Block the source address
Enforce MFA and lockout policies
yaml: title: Failed Network Logon From Non-Internal Address
description: Detects event 4625 with logon type 3 where the source address is not in a private range. Threshold logic belongs in a correlation rule.
condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
- Remote users mistyping passwords over VPNs that do not translate client addresses

rules.objective: Flag failed SSH authentication and invalid-user attempts on Linux hosts.
investigation: Count attempts per source and check for a later 'Accepted' message
Check whether password authentication should be enabled at all
remediation: Disable password authentication (keys only)
Restrict SSH to bastion and VPN ranges
Use fail2ban or equivalent rate limiting
yaml: title: SSH Failed Password or Invalid User
description: Detects sshd messages for failed passwords and unknown users.
- Users mistyping passwords; automation with outdated credentials

rules.objective: Detect common SQL injection probes in web request query strings.
investigation: Check response codes and sizes for the same client (500s, unusually large responses)
Review database logs for errors or unusual queries at the same time
Identify the tool from the user agent
remediation: Fix the vulnerable parameter with parameterised queries
Block the client; add WAF rules as an interim measure
yaml: title: SQL Injection Pattern in URI Query
description: Detects quote characters, boolean tautologies, UNION SELECT and time-based probes in raw or URL-encoded query strings.
- Search fields where users legitimately type apostrophes (names such as O'Brien)

rules.objective: Detect reflected XSS probes in query strings.
investigation: Check whether the response reflected the payload (status code, WAF action)
Look for other probes from the same client
remediation: Ensure output encoding on the affected parameter
Keep a strict Content Security Policy
yaml: title: Cross-Site Scripting Probe in URI Query
description: Detects script tags, javascript URLs and event-handler attributes in raw or URL-encoded query strings.
- Security scanners run by your own team

rules.objective: Detect single outbound sessions sending more than 500 MiB to non-private destinations.
investigation: Identify the source host and process (EDR network telemetry)
Check the destination's reputation and whether the transfer was expected
Determine which data was accessed beforehand
remediation: Block the destination
Apply default-deny egress for servers
Engage legal / DPO if personal data may be involved
yaml: title: Large Outbound Transfer to Non-Private Destination
description: Detects allowed firewall sessions with more than 500 MiB sent to a destination outside private address space.
- Backups to cloud storage and large legitimate uploads (baseline per host)
